title: Mexico Prepares Protocol to Recover and Repatriate Cultural Heritage Located Abroad
author: El Chamuco Staff
content:
_This article by El Chamuco Staff originally appeared in the[November 7, 2026
edition of El Chamuco](https://elchamuco.com.mx/2026/11/07/mexico-prepara-
protocolo-para-recuperar-y-repatriar-patrimonio-cultural-localizado-en-el-
extranjero/), a Mexican political cartoon and news magazine._

**(NOVEMBER 7, 2026).- The Government of Mexico is moving forward in drafting
a protocol to coordinate the recovery and repatriation of Mexican cultural
property located abroad, as well as to strengthen institutional actions
against the illicit trafficking of heritage.**

The Secretariat of Culture, through the National Institute of Anthropology and
History (INAH), the Secretariat of Foreign Affairs (SRE), and the United
Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (Unesco), held the
second working workshop to develop the document called the Protocol for the
Repatriation and Recovery of Cultural Property.

![Archaeological pieces laid out on a table](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/mexico-heritage-repatriation-02-pieces.jpg)Photo: INAH

The meeting took place on November 4, 2026, at the National Museum of History,
located in Chapultepec Castle, with the participation of officials and
specialists from the institutions involved.

INAH's technical secretary, José Luis Perea González, said that the defense
and preservation of cultural heritage requires close collaboration between
institutions to establish mechanisms for protection and repatriation.

![INAH post on X about the protocol](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/mexico-heritage-repatriation-03-inah-post.jpg)INAH
post on X

He explained that the document seeks to build a proposal for an institutional
policy to recover, restitute and repatriate cultural property. He also
highlighted its relationship with the cultural rights of Indigenous and Afro-
Mexican peoples, whose communities promote the conservation of their heritage
through spaces such as community museums and temples.

For his part, INAH's director of World Heritage, Francisco Vidargas Acosta,
explained that the protocol will be a document open to updating as the
problems, contexts and international norms related to the recovery of cultural
property change.

Unesco's national culture officer in Mexico, Carlos Tejada, highlighted the
joint work and noted that eradicating the illicit trafficking of cultural
property is one of the relevant issues of international cooperation.

## What Does the Protocol Include?

The document will consist of ten sections: presentation; general framework and
background; legal and regulatory framework; competent authorities; strategies
and guidelines for action; general course of action; public registry of
cultural property; follow-up, safekeeping and destination; glossary of terms,
and implementation instruments.

![Two ceramic figurines](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/mexico-heritage-repatriation-04-figurines.jpg)Photo:
Secretariat of Culture / INAH

Its scope covers cases in which INAH learns of heritage objects of possible
Mexican origin located in other countries and those that require its
intervention to identify, analyze, document, manage, receive, safeguard or
follow up on them.

Among the scenarios considered are sales and auctions of cultural property, as
well as seizures, confiscations, forfeitures and voluntary handovers that
require a coordinated institutional response.

The work continues the Cooperation Workshop for the Recovery and Repatriation
of Cultural Heritage, held on June 26 and 27, 2025, in Hermosillo, Sonora. At
that meeting, lines of collaboration and exchange of experiences were
established among different areas of INAH, the Secretariat of Foreign Affairs
and Unesco's representation in Mexico.

In the second session, among other officials, INAH's national coordinators of
Archaeology and of Cultural Heritage Conservation, Francisco Mendiola Galván
and Thalía Velasco Castelán, took part, along with representatives of the
institute's centers in seven states in the north of the country and
authorities of the National Museum of History.

![Carved stone head with a headdress](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/mexico-heritage-repatriation-05-head.jpg)Photo: INAH

On behalf of the Secretariat of Foreign Affairs, María José Buerba Romero,
director for the Restitution of Cultural Heritage, and María de Lourdes Ruíz
Pastrana, director of Cultural Diplomacy, took part.

The drafting of the protocol seeks to establish criteria and procedures so
that Mexican institutions act in a coordinated manner when heritage property
is located abroad, and the processes necessary to achieve its recovery.
